title: CLO 2026 Academic Month Silent but Traceable — CLO Empowering Hearing-Impaired Students in Apparel to Explore New Learning and Employment Paths
description: CLO 2026 Official Academic Monthly Course Review Released! Associate Professor Sun Ying from the Department of Fashion and Apparel Design at the College for the Deaf, Tianjin University of Technology, introduced the college’s educational background and teaching realities online, and explained the core value and supportive effects of CLO in professional education for hearing-impaired individuals.
transcript:
Hello, everyone.  
I am Sun Ying, a teacher at the Dragon Art Academy of Tianjin University of Technology.  
Today, I want to share with you the new path for deaf students who have no hearing and no trace of clothing.  
You may have heard of Tianjin University of Technology, but you may not know that there is a Dragon Art Academy of Technology within Tianjin University of Technology.  
Our school specializes in enrolling deaf students.  
Today, I will share with you the situation of our school, an analysis of students’ learning, including how we solve the problem of hearing loss, how they learn the profession of clothing, and how CLO can help them with employment.  
I would like to give you a brief introduction.  
Our school is jointly run by the Tianjin government and the Chinese government.  
It was founded jointly by the Chinese People’s Federation of Disabled Persons.  
It is also the first school in China to recruit deaf students.  
Our predecessor was the Special Education Department of Tianjin University of Technology.  
It was established in 1991 and enrolled the first deaf students.  
In 1997, we officially established the Dragon Art Academy of Technology within Tianjin University of Technology.  
This is an introduction to our school.  
We have about 30 years of experience in teaching.  
Our current majors include clothing and clothing design, product design, visual communication, computer and network engineering, etc.  
In 2001, together with the National Dragon Art Academy of Technology in the United States, the Russian Bauman National Technical University, and the Japanese Judo Technical University of Technology, we jointly launched a network education project related to creating opportunities for deaf people.  
Our students also place great emphasis on external communication.  
We participated in the opening ceremony of the Beijing Chamber of Commerce.  
In 2013, we launched a new model — a comprehensive education model — which allows hearing students to enter the classes and majors of deaf students.  
In 2013, we also expanded our majors to 10 design majors.  
In 2018, we achieved academic recognition for Chinese and American hearing students, including the first deaf student.  
In 2019, we officially obtained the training qualification for hearing and math students.  
In 2015, we also established the Dragon Art Academy of Technology.  
In 2016, we established a new minor major dedicated to the help and support of CLOU, namely non-disabled digital development and sustainable design.  
This is the overall situation of our school.  

Our students are also special.  
So I would like to introduce the situation of our students here.  
Our students are deaf, that is, deaf students.  
Therefore, in terms of learning, they face some difficulties.  
First, there is a lack of information.  
In the classroom, we teach with sign language.  
We teach professional knowledge through sign language.  
However, there is a clear difference between sign language and Chinese.  
This is like the difference between Chinese and English.  
There is a linguistic deviation problem.  
At the same time, they rely mainly on vision to receive information.  
So they may miss some important knowledge points if they lower their heads while learning.  
Or there may be some misunderstanding of the sign language.  
This leads to a reduced absorption rate of knowledge.  
Especially with some abstract concepts and professional vocabulary in clothing, they encounter obstacles in understanding.  

The second difficulty is that our students are deeply aware of the problems in art education.  
Our problem is that these abstract concepts and theories are challenging for deaf students.  
There is a lack of emotion and experience.  
Therefore, they lack an effective connection channel.  
The traditional teaching mode is actually not suitable for us.  
It is not suitable for our students’ learning.  

The third difficulty is that it is hard for them to integrate into society.  
Due to hearing obstacles, they sometimes get misunderstood or face difficulties.  
Especially in the fourth grade, during their internship stage — the stage of finding a job — this problem is quite prominent.  
It is difficult to find relevant professional internship positions.  

But in fact, our students still have many advantages.  
For example, due to their lack of hearing, they are visually sensitive.  
They are also very unique in the field of art.  
They have strong manual dexterity.  
They can compensate for the lack of hearing through touch and vision.  
They are less distracted and very focused.  
They are also patient.  

As for the clothing profession, it is a form of non-verbal expression, right?  
Art is more inclusive.  
So it is actually more suitable for deaf people.  

Therefore, based on the characteristics of our students, we have been exploring and solving breakthrough methods.  
By utilizing visual and tactile learning, these two channels, we increase the absorption rate of knowledge in students.  
For example, we use CLO, LCD, or VR virtual venues, and so on, to create a kind of visualized teaching and immersive interactive experience to solve the problems of deep cognitive and physical difficulties.  

At the same time, in their thinking, we develop a three-layer cognitive structure and improve their theoretical thinking ability, which is also helpful.  
For example, through values, leading to creative thinking and progressive abilities, to transmit professional knowledge.  
I also hope that through technology, we can assist in the cultivation and transformation of traditional culture.  

In the fourth aspect, I will specifically introduce our “negative energy path,” because our students are more special.  
So, in our classroom, I have put two videos showing some teaching scenarios.  
That is, we have to explain professional knowledge through sign language.  
At the same time, there are some real-time language translation systems, that is, subtitles displayed on the screen.  
Mainly, it depends on sign language.  
Therefore, we need to use a multimodal teaching method.  
Through sign language, visual, symbolic, and tactile methods, using materials to convey emotions, so that students can better understand.  
Finally, through creation and experience, they can master knowledge related to clothing and professional vocabulary understanding.  

The second main “negative energy path” is that we have built a production and learning platform through school cooperation.  
In recent years, we have introduced CLO at our school, including the intelligent embroidery system, Xunfei translation software, and so on.  
That is, using technology to provide more space for the teaching of deaf people and the design of clothing professionals.  
So, we must use technology to provide more space and possibilities for teaching deaf students and clothing design professionals.  

Therefore, our online teaching sessions are all about using sign language and then comprehensively applying three-dimensional simulation CLO, and then AI to realize 3D embroidery, serving the teaching of clothing professionals.  

So, let me briefly introduce the specific connection of this path.  
At the end of 2023, we introduced CLO in our class.  
We introduced CLO in our class.  
We introduced CLO in our class.  
So, we immediately developed a new talent training program for students in 2024, and then we integrated CLO into the training system.  

But our students in the 2021, 2022, and 2023 training programs could not use it casually.  
However, we wanted some students to use it earlier and benefit earlier.  
Therefore, we took a more moderate approach.  
In the current training program, we selected some courses without changing the original teaching content.  
In this way, each course compresses 4-8 classes.  
Then, we separately included CLO teaching content in multiple courses.  

For example, in the second grade.  
In the second grade, our main courses are fashion technique, professional industrial knowledge, and fashion structure.  
We integrated CLO into these three courses.  
Then, we learn some basic CLO knowledge separately.  
For example, sewing shirts, pants, simple style changes, the use of 3D pens, etc.  
This is the second-grade class.  

In the third grade, we will connect some special courses.  
For example, currently, we have a computer embroidery class.  
We will integrate CLO and embroidery CAD together.  
Then, use CLO to make a virtual presentation.  
Then, we will use the embroidery machine to produce the finished product.  

Finally, we use AI.  
It is very convenient to use AI to make a small video like this through this training.  
In the third grade, we have some special courses, such as art design, which can be realized with CLO.  

This is what our students did before.  
Before CLO, we were divided into groups to make small pieces.  
Then, CLO was very troublesome.  
It was a small piece and very time-consuming.  
But with CLO, we can make a single blueprint of CLO and make it virtual.  
This greatly improves our learning efficiency.  

We can use the virtual presentation of CLO repeatedly.  
This is extremely helpful to our students because they may need to receive some information repeatedly during class.  
We should watch the videos repeatedly to make it easier for them.  

The most important thing in the fourth year is the graduation design.  
Because many graduate students were not at school at that time, we selected some students who were at school.  
CLOE gave us training, including classroom training, and took the students to attend CLOE's classes together.  
Then we used CLOE in the students’ graduation design at that time.  

In 2025, all students will be able to use CLOE to complete their graduation design, including participating in competitions.  
The design of this outdoor costume is also the result of our students’ participation in the Tianjin fashion competition.  

In addition, because we integrated CLOE into the course, the evaluation system of the entire work was appropriately adjusted, strengthening its visual impact and weakening reliance on hearing, making their thinking more tangible.  
Then, we also adjusted the weighting in the evaluation standards.  

Furthermore, we have also used CLOE to lead students to actively participate in many innovation and entrepreneurship competitions, achieving very good results.  
Including the second digital recovery design competition, we also took students to do the Tang Dynasty Zanhua City Painting, and the third New Year’s Eve painting.  
We basically participated in each of these.  

The last part is about employment.  
In fact, employment for our students is very, very difficult.  
Why do I say this?  
Because first of all, when a deaf person looks for a job and applies with a resume, it may be hard to contact them.  
When companies call them and want to schedule interviews, they may not be able to communicate effectively since they can only send text messages.  

So their internships and employment rely on teachers and schools recommending jobs for them.  
On the other hand, it also relies on promoting employment through the disabled community.  

I would like to express my special gratitude to Shanghai New Year's Eve Cologne.  
Last year when we went back to Cologne, Mr. Zhang introduced the overall situation of Cologne to us.  
We have a student from the class of 2024 who interned at Cologne and then stayed there.  
Cologne provides very good job opportunities for our hearing-impaired students.  
With great tolerance and kindness, they have built a platform for these students to grow, making them more confident on the road to their dreams.  

So, I have summarized the recent employment situation of our students.  
They mainly work in clothing-related jobs, mostly relying on teacher recommendations.  

For example, they have worked as clothing assistants in a clothing company in Guangzhou, doing fashion design of sandalwood, including customization of stage makeup.  
These jobs were all recommended by our teachers.  

Then, there is Cologne’s new washing, specifically making clothing models, including laser cutting, cutting, CAD, and so on.  
For example, this year’s student was recommended to a company in Hebei Province that makes cheongsams.  
At that time, we recommended them for computer embroidery and CAD work.  
Later, the company found that this student could also work with Cologne technology.  
They thought, “Oh, this is great.”  
Their company did not have this technology yet.  
So the boss of that company asked me if I had any other students to recommend.  

In this process, our students have still received very high evaluations from their employers.  

In addition, some students may change jobs, which is inevitable.  
Because the companies they find may be related to clothing, for example, character design, flat surface design such as fashion magazines, these related flat surface designers, including transitions into pattern design, or visiting professionals, also transitions, and some professionals in the field who are good at mobility design.  

I also hope that through this platform today, some related enterprises can see and understand the situation of our hearing-impaired students and be able to provide them with more job opportunities.  

I would like to thank CLO again for building a good platform for our children.  
Thank you, everyone.

chunks.content: # CLO 2026 Academic Month Silent but Traceable — CLO Empowering Hearing-Impaired Students in Apparel to Explore New Learning and Employment Paths ## Introduction to Dragon Art Academy of Tianjin University of Technology This section provides an overview of the Dragon Art Academy of Technology at Tianjin University of Technology, focusing on its specialization in educating deaf students in apparel and design fields, and its historical development. The Dragon Art Academy of Technology, part of Tianjin University of Technology, is a pioneering institution in China dedicated to enrolling and educating deaf students. Founded originally as the Special Education Department in 1991, it formally became the Dragon Art Academy in 1997. The academy is jointly run by the Tianjin government and the Chinese People's Federation of Disabled Persons. With nearly 30 years of experience, it offers majors including clothing and clothing design, product design, visual communication, and computer and network engineering. In 2001, the academy collaborated internationally with institutions such as the National Dragon Art Academy of Technology (USA), Bauman National Technical University (Russia), and Judo Technical University of Technology (Japan) to launch a network education project aimed at creating opportunities for deaf people. In 2013, the academy introduced a comprehensive education model integrating hearing students into deaf students' classes and expanded its design majors to ten. By 2018, academic recognition was achieved for both Chinese and American hearing students, including the first deaf student to be recognized. In 2019, the academy obtained official training qualifications for hearing and math students. A minor in non-disabled digital development and sustainable design was established in 2016, reflecting the academy's commitment to innovative and inclusive education. ## Challenges Faced by Deaf Students in Apparel Education This section addresses the unique learning challenges deaf students encounter in apparel education, including linguistic barriers, abstract concept comprehension, and social integration issues. Deaf students primarily rely on sign language and visual input for learning, which creates a linguistic gap similar to the difference between Chinese and English. This linguistic deviation can lead to misunderstandings and missed information, especially with abstract concepts and specialized vocabulary in clothing design. The students also face difficulties connecting emotionally and experientially with art education due to these abstract theories and traditional teaching methods that do not accommodate their learning needs. Social integration poses another challenge, particularly during internships and job placements in their fourth academic year. Communication barriers often lead to misunderstandings and difficulty finding relevant professional opportunities. Despite these challenges, deaf students have distinct advantages such as heightened visual sensitivity, strong manual dexterity, focused attention, and patience. The non-verbal nature of clothing design and art makes these fields particularly suitable for them. ## Innovative Teaching Approaches Using Technology This section outlines the academy's strategies for overcoming educational barriers by leveraging multimodal teaching methods and advanced technologies like CLO, VR, and AI. The academy has developed breakthrough teaching methods that utilize visual and tactile learning channels to improve knowledge absorption.

chunks.content: Despite these challenges, deaf students have distinct advantages such as heightened visual sensitivity, strong manual dexterity, focused attention, and patience. The non-verbal nature of clothing design and art makes these fields particularly suitable for them. ## Innovative Teaching Approaches Using Technology This section outlines the academy's strategies for overcoming educational barriers by leveraging multimodal teaching methods and advanced technologies like CLO, VR, and AI. The academy has developed breakthrough teaching methods that utilize visual and tactile learning channels to improve knowledge absorption. Technologies such as CLO 3D garment simulation software, LCD displays, and VR immersive environments create visualized and interactive experiences that help students grasp complex concepts. A three-layer cognitive structure is employed to enhance theoretical thinking, progressing from values to creative and progressive abilities, thereby facilitating professional knowledge transmission. Multimodal teaching combines sign language with visual, symbolic, and tactile methods, including real-time language translation and subtitle systems, to accommodate diverse learning needs. Materials are used to convey emotions and deepen understanding, culminating in creative production and experiential learning. The academy has also established a production and learning platform integrating intelligent embroidery systems and Xunfei translation software, expanding the scope for teaching apparel design to hearing-impaired students through technology. ## Integration of CLO Software in Curriculum and Training This section details how CLO software has been introduced and integrated into the academy’s apparel education curriculum to enhance learning efficiency and practical skills. CLO was introduced at the end of 2023, leading to the development of a new talent training program in 2024 that incorporates CLO into the existing curriculum. For students enrolled before CLO’s introduction (2021-2023), selected courses now integrate CLO without altering the core teaching content. In the second year, CLO is integrated into courses like fashion technique, professional industrial knowledge, and fashion structure. Students learn basic CLO skills such as sewing shirts and pants, simple style modifications, and the use of 3D pens. In the third year, CLO is combined with embroidery CAD in specialized courses. Students use CLO for virtual presentations and then produce physical garments using embroidery machines. AI technology supports the creation of training videos, facilitating easier and repeated access to instructional content, which is beneficial given students' need to revisit information multiple times. Before CLO, students worked in groups on small pieces, which was time-consuming. CLO allows the creation of virtual garment blueprints, greatly improving learning efficiency and enabling repeated virtual presentations. ## CLO in Graduation Design and Competitions This section covers the application of CLO in final year projects and competitive events, highlighting its impact on evaluation and student achievements. In the fourth year, CLOE (CLO Education) training was provided through classroom sessions and joint classes with CLOE instructors. Students used CLOE software for their graduation designs starting in 2023, with full implementation planned for all students by 2025. Students have participated in notable competitions such as the Tianjin Fashion Competition, creating designs like outdoor costumes using CLOE.

chunks.title: CLO 2026 Academic Month Silent but Traceable — CLO Empowering Hearing-Impaired Students in Apparel to Explore New Learning and Employment Paths
chunks.content: ## CLO in Graduation Design and Competitions This section covers the application of CLO in final year projects and competitive events, highlighting its impact on evaluation and student achievements. In the fourth year, CLOE (CLO Education) training was provided through classroom sessions and joint classes with CLOE instructors. Students used CLOE software for their graduation designs starting in 2023, with full implementation planned for all students by 2025. Students have participated in notable competitions such as the Tianjin Fashion Competition, creating designs like outdoor costumes using CLOE. The integration of CLOE into coursework led to adjustments in the evaluation system, increasing emphasis on visual impact and reducing reliance on hearing, thus making assessment more accessible and reflective of students’ tangible skills. The academy has supported student participation in innovation and entrepreneurship competitions, including digital recovery design contests and traditional art painting events, achieving commendable results. ## Employment Challenges and Opportunities for Deaf Students This section explores the difficulties deaf students face in employment, the role of teacher and community support, and successful employment cases facilitated by CLO and partnerships. Employment remains a significant challenge due to communication barriers during hiring processes, such as difficulty coordinating interviews via phone calls. Consequently, internships and job placements heavily depend on school and teacher recommendations and promotion within the disabled community. Partnerships with organizations like Shanghai New Year's Eve Cologne provide valuable job opportunities. For example, a 2024 graduate interned and remained employed at Cologne, which offers a tolerant and supportive environment for hearing-impaired individuals. Graduates typically work in clothing-related roles such as clothing assistants, fashion design, stage makeup customization, laser cutting, CAD, and computer embroidery. Notably, some employers have recognized the value of CLO technology skills among graduates, expanding job prospects. Students also transition into related fields like character design, fashion magazine layout, pattern design, and mobility design, demonstrating adaptability. The academy encourages enterprises to better understand and support hearing-impaired talent, highlighting CLO’s role in empowering these students for meaningful employment. ## Conclusion and Acknowledgments The Dragon Art Academy of Tianjin University of Technology continues to innovate in the education and employment of deaf students within apparel design. CLO software and related technologies have significantly enhanced learning, practical skills, and job readiness. The academy expresses gratitude to CLO and partner organizations for providing platforms that nurture students’ growth and confidence in pursuing their career aspirations.
